To the Joint Standing Committee on Labor Hearing, April 16, 2025

Committee on Labor. My name is Dillon Murray, Legislative Liaison for the Maine Department of Labor (Department). I am here today to speak on behalf of the Department in respectful
opposition to LD 1105, "An Act Concerning Displaced Civilian Federal Firefighters in Maine."

We greatly appreciate the sponsor's intent to support civilian federal firefighters affected by
reductions in force or closures at federal facilities. Ensuring smooth transitions for displaced
workers is a goal we share. That said, we believe this bill may be unnecessary given existing
resources, and it raises several implementation concerns we'd like to highlight.

1. Unclear Implementation Mechanism: The bill directs the Department to create and maintain a database of displaced civilian
federal firefighters but does not identify how the Department is to collect that information. if the intent is to use unemployment insurance (Ul) claims, that raises
potential conflicts with confidentiality laws governing Ul data. Additionally, not all
displaced workers file for Ul benefits---some may quickly find otherjobs, retire, or exit the
workforce altogether--meaning the resulting database could be incomplete or
inconsistent.
2. Existing Tools Already Serve This Function: The Department already administers Maine JobLink, a free, publicly available online system where emp|oyers--including municipal fire departments--can postjob openings, and jobseekers can create profiles and apply directly. Displaced federal civilian firefighters are fully eligible to use this platform, and it is already integrated with workforce services
we provide through our Bureau of Employment Services. We believe this existing tool
meets the goals outlined in the bill without requiring new legislation. 3. Resource and Administrative Considerations:
LD 1105 would establish a new database that the Department would be charged with maintaining for a minimum of four years. While the intent is commendable, setting up

Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association
In Opposition to LD 1105, An Act Concerning Displaced Civilian Federal Firefighters in Maine
April 16, 2025
Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder and members of the Labor Committee, my name is Kate Dufour, and I am submitting written testimony in opposition to LD 1105 on behalf of the municipal officials who serve on the Association's Legislative Policy Committee.
Although members of the policy committee appreciate the intent to help fill vacancies in municipal firefighter departments, mandating that fire chiefs give priority consideration to displaced civilian federal fighters is of concern, leading municipal leaders to question the need to upset the apple cart.
While policy committee members recognize that the bill does not require a fire chief to offer a job to a displaced firefighter who does not meet all local requirements, it does elevate those candidates above all others and ignores equally important attributes. From a municipal perspective, the "good standing" provision under section 2 of the bill could have unintended consequences by putting a damper on department morale, derailing succession planning efforts and devaluing the importance of an individual's understanding of the community being served. It could become a public relations nightmare if fire chiefs are required to hire a civilian federal firefighter, despite another firefighter's seniority, career advancement plans, or years of volunteer service.
Additionally, civilian federal firefighters who meet the local standards will already be desired candidates for vacancies; however, the bill broadens this language to include all "open" positions which could be read to include internal department vacancies. A civilian federal firefighter who has served a community on a part-time basis would automatically be elevated for preference of an open supervisor position, instead of a vacancy created and available to all members of the department.
Municipalities already have the tools necessary to hire firefighters who have the right mix of skills, training and community support. Rather than requiring fire chiefs to give priority standing to a category of public service employees, perhaps the database suggested in the bill could be used by fire chiefs as a centralized recruitment tool.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

LD 1105, An Act Concerning Displaced Civilian Federal Firefighters in
Maine
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Labor

Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder and honorable members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Labor, my name is Kristi Mathieson and I have the distinct pleasure of representing the beautiful
seaside community of Kittery, House District 151. I am here to present LD 1105, An Act Concerning
Displaced Civilian Federal Firefighters in Maine.

This bill was brought to me by President of the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard Professional Fire Fighters
IAFF Local F-123, Kyle C. Moser. The intent of this bill is to allow civilian federal firefighters,
working at the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, Naval Computers and Telecommunications Facility in Cutler and the Togus Veteran Affairs Medical Center in Augusta, in the event of an installation closure or reduction, an opportunity for reemployment as municipal firefighter.

These locations employ 72 federal firefighters, many who were born and raised in Maine and others who have moved to the area and built families and homes here because of their employment. These firefighters not only protect the Department of Defense (DOD), the Department of the Navy and Department of Veterans Affairs' assets in the state, but many also serve as volunteer and/or per diem fire/emergency medical services (EMS) persomiel in the municipalities they live.

This bill does not tie the hands of municipal fire chiefs. If anything, it provides the unique opportunity
to hire nationally certified firefighters, emergency medical technicians (EMTS), paramedics,
driver/operators and hazardous materials (HAZMAT) technicians, which are the basic certifications for
all ENTRY level DOD firefighters.

Under this bill, when a federal firefighter is made aware that their job is going to be terminated due to
a closure or reduction in force, they will submit to the Maine Department of Labor (DOL) their name,
contact information, federal service computation date, time in the federal service and a list of all
certifications. The Maine DOL will compile an electronic list of all eligible federal firefighters as
established by the act and submit this list to municipalities actively seeking firefighters. This seemed
like a win-win bill when l spoke about it with President Moser. We also had our fire chief and our town manager in on the discussions. We all agreed we need to keep our highly qualified firefighter workforce in Maine! Please join me in supporting LD 1105.

Testimony of Kyle C. Moser, 5th District Vice President
Professional Fire Fighters of Maine
LD 1105 An Act Concerning Displaced Civilian Federal Firefighters in Maine
Chairman Tipping, Chairwoman Roeder and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Labor, Good morning and thank you for the opportunity to appear before this committee today in support of LD 1105, "An Act Concerning Displaced Civilian Federal Firefighters in Maine".
My name is Kyle Moser, and I am the 5th District Vice President of the Professional Fire Fighters of Maine. I am here today representing the views of our Executive Board and over 1,300 Professional Firefighters, Paramedics, EMTs & Dispatchers. The PFFMaine's 5th District is comprised of all federal and private sector firefighters in the state. I am also a Federal Firefighter at the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard where I have worked for 9 years.
LD 1105 will have a direct effect on the over seventy (70) federal firefighters across Maine. These firefighters are employed by the United States Government they are on first line of emergency response on the ground at locations such as the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard in Kittery, Naval Computers and Telecommunications Area in Cutler, and even the Veteran Affairs Hospital in Togas; having the primary responsibility of engaging in the prevention, control, or extinguishment of fires and response to emergency situations in which life, property, or the environment is at risk, including the prevention, control, suppression, or management of wildland fires on military installations and other federal properties.
The intent and purpose behind this bill is to allow federal firefighters, in the event of a reduction in force or an installation closure, an easier opportunity to gain employment as municipal firefighters in the State. First and foremost, if this bill is enacted into law, I sincerely hope it never has to used. If this is being used, that means fire protection has been reduced or an installation has been completely closed, and thus many federal employees including firefighters have lost jobs. Many of these firefighters who were born and raised in Maine and others who have moved to the area and have built families and homes here because of their employment will need a job to continue to take care of their families.
Federal firefighters are some of the most highly trained in the country. Our basic certifications to hold any position, such as firefighter, fire captain, or chief fire officer far exceed what most public sector fire departments require. Our certifications are nationally recognized, we are EMTs and Paramedics and hold high level security clearances and go through extensive criminal background checks.
1

This bill if enacted and ever needed to be utilized would not only put peace of mind for federal firefighters here in Maine, it is also a great opportunity for Public Sector Fire Chiefs and Municipalities. Maine Fire Chiefs would have the ability to hire highly trained and qualified individuals, thus saving the taxpayers money when compared to having to hire someone with no training or certifications. This bill does not look to undermine any municipalities hiring practices; rather, it serves as a safety net for federal firefighters in Maine, ensuring support if they lose their jobs in the federal sector due to circumstances beyond their control. Measures such as this one proposed have been successfully accomplished in other States, most notably in New Jersey, and other actions to protect federal firefighters have also been successful in Massachusetts and California. The Professional Fire Fighters of Maine are in full support of this piece of legislation. We ask you for your support in passing LD 1105 to ensure Federal Firefighters in the State of Maine have a safeguard for employment as firefighters. Thank you for your time and attention. I would be happy to address any questions you may have. Respectfully Submitted on this day, Thursday, April 16th, 2025. Kyle C. LD 1105 An Act Concerning Displaced Civilian Federal Firefighters in Maine
Good morning, Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder and esteemed members of the Labor Committee. Thank you for the opportunity to speak to you this morning on the important legislation known as LD 1105, An Act Concerning Displaced Civilian Federal Firefighters in Maine which seeks to establish vital support mechanisms for displaced civilian federal firefighters across the State of Maine working at the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, Naval Computers & Telecommunications Facility in Cutler and the Veteran Affairs Hospital in Togas.
My name is Michael J. Crouse, a resident of Kittery, Maine, and I have dedicated over 45 years of my life to advocating for the rights and working conditions of firefighters across North America. As the IAFF's 16th District Vice President, and now as Vice President Emeritus, I have represented the IAFF's federal firefighters throughout North America. Drawing from my extensive experience, particularly during the challenging times of the federal government's Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) process, I stand in full support of LD 1105.
Throughout my career, I have witnessed firsthand the detrimental impact that federal base closures and consequent layoffs have on our brave civilian federal firefighters. In particular, the BRAC process, which impacted over 700 federal firefighters, along with the pending attacks on federal employees as of late has underscored the necessity for immediate intervention and support structures as we prepare for the potential of future layoffs, reductions in force actions, base realignments or even another round of base closures as DOD continues to look for ways to cut costs. The need for effective policy measures that facilitate the placement of these dedicated federal firefighters into vacant municipal roles cannot be overstated.
In light of these past experiences, LD 1105 represents a significant step forward in ensuring that displaced federal firefighters are not left without options or resources in the wake of their potential job losses. The planned establishment of a database to maintain a record of displaced qualified civilian federal firefighters is a groundbreaking initiative here in Maine. It echoes the concerns and struggles many have faced during the turbulence of layoffs, realignments and closures, providing a lifeline for those who have bravely served our communities and the nation.

The database will allow Maine to efficiently connect displaced federal firefighters with municipalities seeking to fill open (vacant) Fire/EMS positions. By prioritizing these dedicated civil servants, we acknowledge their years of service, specialized training, and commitment to public safety. These federal firefighters not only protect the Department of Defense (DOD), Department of the Navy (DON), and Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) assets in the state, but they also work closely with municipal and volunteer fire departments outside of these facilities. Many of these firefighters also serve as volunteer and/or per diem Fire/EMS personnel. This measure not only empowers municipalities to make informed hiring decisions but also serves as a testament to our collective recognition of the sacrifices made by these federal firefighters during their service to our country.
Moreover, LD 1105's provision for giving priority consideration to displaced civilian federal firefighters for up to 48 months post-termination reflects a fair and just approach to employment support. In working with local fire chiefs to include these displaced firefighters in the hiring process, we are not just offering jobs; we are providing a pathway back into a profession that requires courage and skill, aligning with the firefighters' fight to serve their communities once again.
Equally important is the bill's focus on regionality, giving first consideration to displaced firefighters residing in the municipalities or counties where the jobs are located. This targeted approach ensures that we are not only retaining skilled fire service professionals locally but also that community's benefit from the expertise and dedication these individuals bring.
I cannot emphasize enough the responsibility we hold to care for those who protect us. Supporting LD 1105 is not just about legislation; it is about safeguarding a legacy of service, ensuring that the sacrifices made by federal firefighters are honored through meaningful opportunities in municipal fire departments. This bill is a forward-thinking solution that also stands as a pillar of our mutual commitment to public safety and the welfare of our firefighters and their families.
In conclusion, I respectfully urge all members of the committee to support that passage of LD 1105. Our civilian federal firefighters always have and will continue to stand ready to respond to emergencies on their respective facilities and to Maine communities under their respective MutualAid agreements, and it is now our duty to respond to their needs should the federal government start abolishing the federal firefighter positions working in the State of Maine . Together, we can create a framework that not only addresses current challenges but also anticipates future opportunities. Thank you for your attention, and I look forward to our collective efforts in supporting this vital legislation.
Sincerely,
Michael

Testimony of Representative Michele Meyer in support of
LD 1105, An Act Concerning Displaced Civilian Federal

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Labor
Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder and esteemed members of the Labor Committee, I am
Michele Meyer. I represent the people of southern Maine's District 150, all of Eliot and parts of
Kittery and South Berwick. Among them are courageous federal firefighters at the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, as well as our dedicated volunteer and public sector firefighters throughout my
district. Thank you for the opportunity to express my strong support for LD 1105, An Act
Concerning Displaced Civilian Federal Firefighters in Maine.
LD 1105 provides essential support for displaced civilian federal firefighters in Maine,
specifically those associated with Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, the Naval Computers and
Telecommunications Facility in Cutler, and Togus VA Medical Center.

Federal firefighters play a crucial role in safeguarding our communities and the environment from fire risks and other threats to public safety. The firefighters at Portsmouth Naval Shipyard lead efforts in fire prevention, suppression, and emergency medical response. They protect both the facility and the surrounding communities, participating in Fire/EMS Mutual Aid Programs
across Southern Maine and in New Hampshire.
The rigorous qualifications and training requirements established by the federal govermnent -
including physical fitness, certifications and background checks -- ensure that federal firefighters meet high standards of excellence necessary for this demanding profession. Additionally, the Department of Defense's Fire and Emergency Services Certification Program emphasizes the need for continuous education and specialized training. This guarantees that firefighters can effectively handle a wide range of challenges in an evolving field.

District 150: Eliot, Kittery (part) and South Berwick (part)

Transitioning displaced federal firefighters into local fire and public safety departments in Maine, as this bill would facilitate, provides significant benefits. These firefighters bring extensive training and experience that can enhance community safety and ensure continuity of services. Their familiarity with local risks and protocols helps maintain uninterrupted emergency services, which is vital for public safety.
These facts make hiring displaced firefighters offers a cost-effective staffing solution for local
departments, as they require less on-the-j ob training and can immediately contribute to operational efficiency. Their integration fosters community trust and enhances departmental capacity, leading to faster response times and more effective emergency medical services. This transition also addresses staffing shortages and retains committed public servants within the firefighting profession. It cultivates opportunities for collaborative training, enhancing the skills of all personnel to tackle diverse risks.
A strong fire and public safety presence is essential for community resilience, especially in the
face of climate change and emerging threats. By transitioning these experienced federal firefighters to local roles, we can improve community preparedness and response capabilities. Supporting this transition demonstrates our commitment to our public servants, many of whom have also served our country in the military, and boosts morale among public safety personnel.
LD 1105 facilitates a smooth transition for federal firefighters into Maine's public safety
departments, enhancing community safety while allowing these dedicated individuals to continue their service. I urge you to support this important legislation to ensure they have the tools, resources, and recognition they deserve. Thank you for your consideration.

Distinguished Members of The Joint Standing Committee on Labor,

My name is Scott Lizotte, President of IAFF Local F-316, representing federal firefighters at NSA Cutler, Maine who dedicate their lives to keeping Maine's communities and naval infrastructure safe. I stand before you today with a heavy heart but unwavering hope, urging your support for LD 1105: AN ACT CONCERNING DISPLACED CIVILIAN FEDERAL FIREFIGHTERS IN MAINE.

Picture a firefighter, exhausted from battling flames, returning home to face a different kind of fear: the threat of job loss due to federal workforce reductions. This is the reality for Maine's federal firefighters in this current political climate. These brave men and women, who risk everything to protect us, live with the dread of displacement, wondering how they'll provide for their families. Parents lie awake, hearts racing, knowing their children may face uprooted lives, new schools, lost friends, and shattered stability. The emotional toll is devastating, yet they lace up their boots and serve day after day.

LD 1105 is their lifeline. By creating a priority hiring list for displaced federal firefighters, this bill ensures their expertise strengthens Maine's municipal fire departments. These are not just skilled professionals; they are pillars of our communities', fathers, mothers, and neighbors who deserve a chance to stay and serve. Without this legislation, we risk losing them to other states, weakening our fire services and leaving families in despair.

California has shown the way with its Displaced Firefighter List, managed by the California Fire Fighter Joint Apprenticeship Committee. This program helps displaced firefighters, including federal civilians, continue their careers by connecting them with hiring departments, saving time and preserving talent. Maine can follow this proven model, becoming a national leader in supporting those who protect us.

On behalf of IAFF Local F-316, I implore you to pass LD 1105. Let's give our firefighters the security they've earned, so they can focus on saving lives without fearing for their families' futures. Thank you for standing with those who stand for us.
